question: Jab koi shakhs mashkook halaat mein foat ho jaye, to police ko maut ki wajah ki baaqaida tehqeeqaat karni hoti hai — kya hamara system yeh kahin darj karta hai, khaas tor par jab hamare itne cases mein maut shamil hai?
served_answer:
### 1. Governing Provision and Its Substance:
The law requires that when a person dies under suspicious circumstances, the police must conduct a thorough investigation into the cause of death. This is outlined in **Section 174 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Pakistan)**, which mandates that the police inquire and report on suicide, unnatural death, or any other suspicious death. Additionally, **Rule 25.31 of the Punjab Police Rules (III)** specifies that the officer in charge of the police station must immediately inform the nearest magistrate authorized to hold inquests and conduct an investigation in the manner prescribed by Section 174 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

### 2. What Our Case Records Actually Show:
According to **our own case records (Document 7)**, out of **73 FIRs** that carry a recorded section cite, **10 of them** are linked to **PPC §302**, which pertains to murder. This indicates that **murder cases** (which fall under suspicious deaths) are indeed recorded in our system. However, the summary does not provide specific details about whether the police conducted thorough investigations into the cause of death in these cases, nor does it indicate whether the required reports (such as the plan of the scene of death, inventory of clothing, etc.) were prepared and submitted as required under **Punjab Police Rules-III (Document 2)**.

In conclusion, while our system does record cases involving suspicious deaths, the summary does not confirm whether the full investigative procedures required by law were followed in these cases.

question: Jab koi shakhs mashkook halaat mein foat ho jaye, to police ko maut ki wajah ki baaqaida tehqeeqaat karni hoti hai — kya hamara system yeh kahin darj karta hai, khaas tor par jab hamare itne cases mein maut shamil hai?
served_answer:
### Legal Requirement:
According to the **Code of Criminal Procedure (Pakistan)**, when a person dies while in the custody of the police or in certain other circumstances (such as unnatural or sudden death), the police are required to conduct an inquiry into the cause of death. This is outlined in **Section 174** and **Section 176** of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which mandate that the police inquire and report on suicide, etc., and that a magistrate may hold an inquiry into the cause of death. The police must also prepare a detailed report that includes the apparent cause of death, descriptions of any injuries, and other relevant information, as specified in **Punjab Police Rules-III** (Document 2). These provisions ensure that the cause of death is thoroughly investigated and documented.

### Case Records Summary:
According to **our own case records (Document 7)**, out of **73 FIRs** that carry a recorded section cite, **10 of them** are linked to **PPC §302** (murder). This indicates that **murder** is a significant category among the cases recorded in the system. However, the summary does not explicitly state how many of these cases involved **inquiries into the cause of death** or whether the **police conducted detailed investigations** as required by law. The summary does not include specific data on whether the police conducted inquiries or prepared detailed reports on deaths, as required by the law.

### Conclusion:
While the law clearly requires the police to investigate and document the cause of death in cases of unnatural or suspicious deaths, the case records do not provide specific data on how many such investigations were conducted or how thoroughly they were documented. The system does not explicitly track or report the number of cases where the police conducted inquiries into the cause of death, despite the legal requirement.

The summary also does not mention whether the police prepared the required reports (such as those outlined in **Document 2**) or whether they followed the procedures outlined in **Section 174** of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

In summary, while the law requires a full investigation into the cause of death in suspicious cases, the case records do not provide enough detail to confirm whether this was consistently done in the 10 murder cases or in other cases involving unnatural death.

question: Jab koi shakhs mashkook halaat mein foat ho jaye, to police ko maut ki wajah ki baaqaida tehqeeqaat karni hoti hai — kya hamara system yeh kahin darj karta hai, khaas tor par jab hamare itne cases mein maut shamil hai?
served_answer:
### Law and Guidelines:
Under the **Code of Criminal Procedure (Pakistan)**, when a person dies while in the custody of the police or under unnatural circumstances, the police are required to conduct an inquiry into the cause of death. This is outlined in **Section 174** of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which mandates that the police inquire and report on suicide, unnatural death, or death under suspicious circumstances. Additionally, **Section 176** provides that a magistrate may hold an inquiry into the cause of death, and the police must report on the cause of death, including the apparent cause, marks of violence, and other relevant details, as specified in **Punjab Police Rules-III** (Document 2).

### Case Records:
According to **our own case records** (Document 7), out of **73 FIRs** that carry a recorded section cite, **10 FIRs** are linked to **PPC §302** (murder). This indicates that **murder cases** are among the most serious and are recorded in the system. However, the data does not explicitly state how many of these cases involve **inquiries into the cause of death** as required by law. The system does record FIRs and section citations, but it does not provide a field or specific data point that explicitly tracks whether the **police conducted an inquiry into the cause of death** in each case, as required by law.

Thus, while the system does record **murder cases**, it does **not specifically track** whether the **inquiry into the cause of death** was conducted in each case.

Rule 25.30

25.30.  Place of trial. - With regard to the place of trial of cases falling under Sections 179-183, Code of Criminal Procedure, police officers shall act solely with reference to the public convenience.

Ordinarily such cases shall be sent up for trial in the district in which the witnesses can attend with the least inconvenience to themselves.
